decision: Centralize authorization policy in one policy layer
reason:
Authorization checks had drifted across controllers, jobs, and command handlers, producing different answers for the same action. A single policy layer gives every entry point one shared contract and one place to test rules.

Adopting it requires coordinated changes across modules, while reversing it would redistribute security logic and recreate audit gaps. This architectural choice should remain visible to future maintainers.
tradeoff: Callers depend on the policy layer and simple checks require an extra indirection.

facets.label: Scope
facets.text: Controllers, jobs, and command handlers share the policy contract.

facets.label: Reversibility
facets.text: Undoing the choice requires redistributing and re-auditing authorization rules.
